head: a3d3860b11a3e6f3846ee455bb5197b9d115779f
summary: I finished resolving the in-progress merge of uat (2e089a1, which brings in SL-040) into slice/SL-042 in the working tree. The only textual conflict was the class remarks in ScanStore.cs. The resolution keeps SL-040's paragraph (raw Size and OnDisk made internal) and follows it with SL-042's paragraph on the rollups. The reflect step's 'imminent defect' was real. SL-040's LargestFilesScaleTests built a hardlink duplicate by passing HardlinkDuplicate to Append. The merged store clears that flag, so those names were charged 1 TB and took the top of the list, and the test failed exactly that way when I put the original line back. It now builds the duplicate as a later name of the preceding file, with the same ID and in the same folder. LargestFiles itself needed no change, because it reads only ChargedSize and ChargedOnDisk of Files. All 199 Core.Tests pass on the merged tree in Release, including the counting-rule tests on real temp trees, the rollup timing test and SL-040's tests. The merged app scans C:\Windows correctly through --report. Per the engine's rules I did not stage or commit. MERGE_HEAD is still set and the index still marks ScanStore.cs unmerged (UU), so the commit step must add it, which concludes the merge.

deviations: I did not commit and did not run `git add`. The sending-back asked the builder to finish the merge and commit, but this stage's standing rules forbid commits and version-control changes. The conflict is resolved in the working tree and no markers remain, but the index still records src/FsAnalyser.Core/Store/ScanStore.cs as unmerged (UU) and MERGE_HEAD is 2e089a1. The commit step must stage it (git add of that path, or add -A); committing then concludes the merge with both parents.
follow_ups: plants.json row F17, added by SL-040, notes that its planted text was 'copied from Scanner.cs:267'. SL-042 removed that line from Scanner.cs. The plant inserts into LargestFiles.cs and does not depend on Scanner.cs, so the harness is unaffected, but the note now points at a line that no longer exists.
